article_title: Confirming Correct, Missing the Rest: LLM Tutoring Agents Struggle Where Feedback Matters Most
citation: Tahreem Yasir, Wenbo Li, Sam Gilson, Sutapa Dey Tithi, Xiaoyi Tian, Tiffany Barnes. (2026). Confirming Correct, Missing the Rest: LLM Tutoring Agents Struggle Where Feedback Matters Most. arXiv:2605.16207. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16207
title: KG-grounded benchmark of 10,836 solution-feedback pairs for step-level LLM tutoring evaluation
description: The article introduces what it calls "the first benchmark for step-level evaluation of LLM tutoring feedback across multiple valid solution paths." It is built from 516 unique proof states drawn from 32 proof problems across five practice levels of a propositional logic tutor deployed in an undergraduate Discrete Mathematics course, with LLM-simulated next-step solutions and reasoning traces. The article reports that "we evaluate 10,836 LLM- simulated next-step solutions and their feedback with KG-grounded evaluation across seven mod- els and three feedback conditions." Code and data are released in a public repository.
requirements: LLM-simulated student solutions with reasoning traces, because the tutoring system logs lack reasoning traces needed for step-level reasoning evaluation
constraints: Proof states come from a single undergraduate Discrete Mathematics course at one institution, which the authors state limits the diversity of reasoning contexts and problem types
target_learning_goals: step-level propositional logic proof diagnosis and feedback evaluation
examples: Each of seven models served as both student simulator generating solutions for all 516 proof states and feedback agent evaluating all solutions under three conditions
